title: Unix and the Origins of the Shell (1969)
explainer: The command-line interface traces back to Unix, begun in 1969 at Bell Labs by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie after the lab stepped back from the much larger, more complex Multics project. Many habits a command line still rewards today — small single-purpose programs, plain text as the universal interchange format, a hierarchical tree of directories — were deliberate design choices made on a spare PDP-7 computer, not accidents of history, and they shaped every Unix-like shell, including the terminals in Linux and macOS used today.
